memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
The LORD said to Moses, "The tenth day of this seventh month is the
Day of Atonement. Hold a sacred assembly and deny yourselves, and
present a food offering to the LORD" - Lev 23:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once a year, everything came to a halt for the Day of Atonement. This
was the day the high priest entered the Most Holy Place with blood, to
make atonement for the sins of the entire nation. Israel was told to
deny themselves - to fast and humble their hearts before God.

There was no celebration in it. Just honest, sober acknowledgment: we
are sinners, and we need covering.

Dear reader, our culture is uncomfortable with this kind of honesty. We
prefer to explain, excuse and move on quickly. But there is a real
freedom in stopping long enough to say, without softening it, "God, I
have sinned."

David wrote that a broken and contrite heart God will not despise (Ps
51:17). James says to humble yourself before the Lord, and He will lift
you up (Jas 4:10). The lifting comes after the humbling, not instead of
it.

And here is the glory of the gospel. Hebrews tells us Christ did not
enter a sanctuary made with human hands; He entered heaven itself, now
to appear for us in God's presence (Heb 9:24). He did it once. Not
every year. Once, and it was enough.

Come honestly. The atonement is finished.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did I last take real, unhurried time to confess sin honestly?
2. Do I rush past my sin instead of bringing it to God?
3. How does Christ's once-for-all atonement free me from fear?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, I stop and admit my sin honestly before You. Thank You that
Jesus has already made full atonement, and I need not carry this guilt.
Amen.
